Unctuous

/UHNGK-choo-uhs/ - the stress falls on UHNGK · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Unctuous means excessively flattering in an insincere, oily way.

The talent scout turned unctuous the moment the girl missed her note, praising her 'bold interpretation.'

Worked Example

At the open house, the listing agent was unctuous from the doorbell on: our coats were 'couture,' our questions 'brilliant,' the sagging porch 'a craftsman's opportunity'—each compliment slicked on to move us one room closer to an offer.

Unctuous keeps the oil in the flattery: where 'flattering' can be warm and 'fawning' can be sincere, unctuous praise coats its target for a purpose, and everyone but the flatterer can feel the grease.

How Unctuous Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

oily

oily: the same slick insincerity, in one everyday word

smarmy

smarmy: informal: ingratiating in a way that makes the skin crawl

Antonyms

sincere

sincere: meaning every word, with nothing performed

plainspoken

plainspoken: saying it straight, without polish or flattery

How Strong Is It? — fawning → unctuous → groveling

fawning vs. unctuous

fawning vs. unctuous: Fawning stops short of unctuous — the fawning admirer is at least sincerely starstruck, while unctuous praise is oil applied with a purpose.

groveling vs. unctuous

groveling vs. unctuous: Groveling goes further than unctuous — groveling drops the polish entirely and simply begs.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of unctuous.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — unctu-

Root — unctu-: anointing oil (Latin unguere/unctus, to anoint)

Suffix — -ous

Suffix — -ous: full of

Put it together

Put it together: Unctu- (anointing oil) + -ous = full of oil. Latin unguere, 'to anoint or rub with oil,' also gives English ointment. Unctuous once literally meant greasy to the touch; the flattery sense keeps the texture — praise so oily it leaves a film.

Use the root in a new word: ointment

Use the root in a new word: ointment: The nurse spread a cooling ointment over the sunburn before wrapping it.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / contemptuous

Unctuous is the connoisseur's insult for flattery with an agenda — you can hear the oil in it. Plain 'insincere' misses the texture. You will also meet obsequious in this unit's reading: the obsequious over-comply and agree with everything, while the unctuous pour on the praise itself.
